v2.note: Direction-symmetric judgment rules (PROMPT_PROGRAM.md cmm round 1): v1 rule 3 ("based ONLY on what is audible") is one-directional and wrong for the 329 SEE questions (audio-stream leak -> 40 residual FP, FPR 0.206, median margin_adj +0.48); on the 392 HEAR questions the visual stream props Yes (61 residual FN, 52 greedy-Yes flipped to No, d_cf_video median -1.4..-3.1). v2: SEE<-video / HEAR<-audio verb-matched rules, sight never creates sound and sound never creates sight, mirror commitment clause. User template byte-identical to v1.

v3.note: Evidence-identity calibration (round 2): v2 killed the cross-modal leak (SEE FP 8->0, HEAR TPR 0.537->0.756) but swapped the error mass -- 13 HEAR FP (ambient/related sound taken for the named one: fan blowing x3, motorcycle revving x2, sheep bleating x2, cat meowing x2; 11/13 were No under v1) and 10 SEE FN (small/diffuse objects lost to "clearly visible": rain, bee, door; 6/10 were Yes under v1). v3: SEE leniency on identity (object itself, even small/brief/partial), HEAR strictness on identity (exact named action; related sound/background hum/same-source noise = No), "answer Yes firmly" dropped. User template still byte-identical to v1.

v4.note: Percept-provenance commitment on HEAR (round 3): v3 left HEAR at TPR 0.683 / FPR 0.179 vs SEE 0.912 / 0.102. Of the 17 dev HEAR items with model-lean-Yes forced to No, 9 saves (gt=no, delta from d_cf_video with d_cf_audio~0 -- expected-not-heard sounds like fan blowing) vs 8 breaks (gt=yes, genuine d_cf_audio -1.1..-2.6, margin_adj -0.18..-0.77 in 6/8). v4 rule 2 adds the provenance split: faint/brief/distant but genuinely heard = Yes; expected-from-the-scene but not heard = No. All else byte-identical to v3.

v5.note: Symmetric commitment completion (round 4): v3 rule 1 (SEE) carries "Answer Yes as soon as the object is visible ... even if small" -> SEE TPR 0.912, while rule 2 (HEAR) carried only the necessary-condition bar "only if identifiable" -> HEAR TPR 0.683 with 8 dev breaks holding genuine audio evidence (d_cf_audio -1.1..-2.6). v5 gives rule 2 the mirror commitment (as soon as identifiable, even if faint/brief/partial). Identity gate and all else byte-identical to v3.

v6.note: Question-type conditional routing of the oracle hybrid (round 5, coordinator endgame; no dev -- dev was shown to favor recall-boosting wording that does not replicate). Offline hybrid (v3 rows on SEE + v1 rows on HEAR) = 77.66/0.626, paired vs v1 fix 22 / break 9, p=0.029, while uniform v3 75.72/0.586 and v5 74.96/0.566 both regressed. Single system prompt: SEE branch = v3 rule 1 verbatim (the piece that transferred: SEE subgroup 78.47->81.37, FPR 0.206->0.108); HEAR branch = v1 rule 3 + rule 1 sentences verbatim; header/format/example byte-identical to v1. Pre-registered full-721 gate: F1 > 76.36 AND Youden >= 0.600 AND paired significance vs v1.

v2.note: Output-contract repair (TRAJECTORY_ANALYSIS.md §7.3/§7.4 D1+D2): minimum complete-sentence answer (≥8 words, ≤5-word replies banned: 122/365 v1 answers were ≤5 words vs gt 18.6) + fixed avoidance template "There is no X visible in this image." for non-visible objects (direct answer on unanswerable items scored F1 18.0 vs 30.6 when avoided).

v3.note: P3 lever (TRAJECTORY_ANALYSIS.md §8.2), PROMPT_PROGRAM round 1: sentence-pattern echo (rebuild the answer from the question's own object/location/medium words — pass-through cell misses gt question-tail nouns, not length) + counting complete sentences ("How many" must yield "There are N <question words>.", number as a word; 8/31 counting items were wrongly answered with the absence template) + anti-false-avoidance (absence template demoted from rule 2 to rule 5; 10/54 gt-affirmative pass-through items got F1≈0 absence answers). Supersedes the legacy unused "meticulous visual auditor" v3 user template.

v4.note: Round 2 (precision/brevity): v3 failed its dev gate (dev -0.98pp, pass-through cell 50.03->44.45); trajectory autopsy showed sampled rollouts padded with un-asked scenery (gt content-word mass ~6, every extra noun is precision loss) and useless "In the photo," openers. v4 rewrites the echo rule as subject+asked-attribute-only with an 8-12 word window and hard one-sentence cap; keeps v3 counting rule and anti-false-avoidance.
